CHAPTER XI
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 35
(1) The community may participate in the implementation of protection and Empowerment of Women.
(2) Participation.............
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be realized through:
a. actions to provide information and/or report Violence Against Women to law enforcement or the authorities, or participate in handling acts of Violence Against Women; and/or
b. provision of communication, information, and education media regarding empowerment and prevention of Violence Against Women within the Family, Community, educational institutions, and public spaces.

Article 18
Empowerment of Women in the social and cultural field is implemented through: increasing knowledge, attitudes and skills to encourage:
a. fulfillment of education in stages according to potential to improve social status;
increasing awareness, willingness, and ability to overcome:
b. health problems through quality promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts primarily in the field of reproductive health;
increasing awareness and knowledge about:
c. independent, healthy and prosperous family planning, including access to consultation services and marriage registration; and
facilitation and efforts to preserve customs and the development of science, knowledge, technology, arts and culture for the advancement of women.
d. facilitation and efforts to preserve customs and the development of science, knowledge, technology, arts and culture for the advancement of women.

CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 25
(1) Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the protection and Empowerment of Women.
(2) Efforts for protection and Empowerment of Women as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs, and activities.
(3) Efforts for protection and Empowerment of Women as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 20
(1) Women's Empowerment in the field of law includes:
a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the field of law through communication, information, and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.
(2) Women's Empowerment in the field of law as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 28
(1) The formulation of policy for planning programs and activities as referred to in Article 27 letter a, is implemented consisting of:
 a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data;
 b. coordination and synchronization of the preparation of planning programs and activities with related Regional Apparatus; and
 c. determination of programs and activities in planning documents.
(2) The formulation of policy for planning programs and activities is further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures.
(3) The formulation of policy for planning programs and activities for the implementation of protection and Empowerment of Women, is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of planning.
(4) The budgeting of programs and activities as referred to in Article 27 letter b, is implemented through general budget policy which is set forth in the Regional revenue and expenditure budget.
(5) The implementation of programs and activities as referred to in Article 27 letter c, is implemented consisting of:
 a. implementation of programs and activities as set forth in the budget document of the Regional Apparatus work unit;
 b. coordination and synchronization of the implementation of activity programs with the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and child protection.
(6) The implementation of monitoring, evaluation, and reporting as referred to in Article 27 letter d, is implemented consisting of:
 a. conducting monitoring and evaluation periodically on the implementation of programs and activities that have been implemented;
 b. making reports periodically; and
 c. evaluation results as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the following year.

CHAPTER VII
MECHANISM FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S PROTECTION AND
EMPOWERMENT
Article 27
The mechanism for the implementation of Women's Protection and Empowerment is carried out through the following stages:
a. formulation of policy planning for programs and activities; b. budgeting of programs and activities;
c. implementation of programs and activities; and
d. monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.

Article 3
The Protection and Empowerment of Women aims to: a. increase the participation of women in the development process; b. improve the quality of life of women;
c. provide guarantees to women in the fulfillment of rights as human beings; and
d. provide a sense of security by increasing protection for women from various acts of violence.

Article 22
(1) Women have the right to obtain health services in order to undergo reproductive life and sexual life that is healthy, safe, and free from coercion and/or violence.
(2) Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
   a. health services for the period before pregnancy, during pregnancy, childbirth, and after giving birth;
   b. pregnancy regulation, contraceptive services, and sexual health; and
   c. reproductive health services.
(3) Health services as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented through promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative approaches.

Article 9
(1) The implementation of protection for women with Disabilities in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of Discrimination includes, among others, freedom from cruel, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity and freedom from exploitation.
(2) Women with Disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall receive the right to protection for:
 a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development;
 b. participation in the fields of education, health, employment, politics, sports, arts and culture as well as utilization of information and communication technology;
 c. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and
 d. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 21
(1) Women's Empowerment in the field of education is carried out through the provision of formal and nonformal education for women in the Region.
(2) Women's Empowerment in the field of education as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to improve the capabilities of women.
(3) Nonformal education as referred to in paragraph (1) includes Women's Empowerment education, skills education, and job training.
(4) Women's Empowerment in the field of education is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XII
FUNDING
Article 36
Funding, implementation of policies, and activity programs for the Protection and Empowerment of Women are sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and other legitimate and non-binding sources of funds.

CHAPTER VI
STRATEGY FOR THE PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
Article 26
(1) The Protection and Empowerment of Women is implemented by integrating Gender mainstreaming and Gender-disaggregated data in an integrated manner based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) The Protection and Empowerment of Women is coordinated by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "the principle of respect for Human Rights" is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women's rights as part of Human Rights.
Letter b What is meant by "the principle of justice and Gender Equality" is that in implementing the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and equality between men and women.
Letter c What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination" is that in the protection and empowerment of women it is carried out without regard to differences whether in the dimension of territory (disaster areas, conflict areas, border areas, underdeveloped areas, remote areas, and others), the dimension of age (productive age, elderly age, and others), and special dimensions (persons with disabilities, workers, and others).
Letter d What is meant by "the principle of victim protection" is that the protection and empowerment of women carried out by the Regional Government, business entities or the community is oriented towards the protection of women as victims.

4.2.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 38 explicitly mandates outreach/education activities: (a) “memberikan sosialisasi kepada Masyarakat dan dunia usaha mengenai kebijakan perlindungan dan Pemberdayaan Perempuan” and (b) providing and disseminating “buku, leaflet, brosur mengenai perlindungan dan Pemberdayaan Perempuan, dan isu-isu terkait lainnya”. This is clearly an education/awareness-raising measure tied to women’s protection/empowerment (which is grounded in gender equality principles in Pasal 2). The judge’s cited English snippet accurately reflects Pasal 38. Therefore a “Yes” is supportable from the policy text, making the golden “No” likely incorrect.

4.3.evaluator_rationale: While the policy mentions providing information and education regarding prevention of violence against women and socialization about protection/empowerment policies, none of the provided sentences explicitly indicate education or awareness activities specifically about laws and policies on violence against women.

Although there are guarantees in laws and regulations that protect citizens, especially women, cases involving women continue to increase, not decrease, because cases of violence against women are like an iceberg phenomenon, namely cases reported to women's protection institutions are only a small part of the actual cases. Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families, so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation are expensive. 4.3.rationale: The retrieved English candidates DO contain explicit awareness/education related to violence against women laws/policies. In the original Indonesian preamble (“Mengingat”), the regulation explicitly references “Undang-Undang Nomor 23 Tahun 2004 tentang Penghapusan Kekerasan Dalam Rumah Tangga” (a key VAW/DV law). Also, Pasal 20(1) provides for “peningkatan kesadaran dan pengetahuan di bidang hukum melalui layanan komunikasi, informasi, dan edukasi” and Pasal 35(2)(b) provides “media komunikasi, informasi, dan edukasi … pencegahan Kekerasan Terhadap Perempuan”. These passages were retrieved ([4.3-2], [4.3-44], [4.3-67]). The judge incorrectly required a sentence that explicitly says ‘education about laws/policies on VAW’ and overlooked that the regulation both (i) cites the VAW-related law and (ii) mandates legal awareness/education and VAW-prevention education media. So the error is primarily judge reasoning, not retrieval/translation.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BOYOLALI REGENCY
NUMBER YEAR 2021
CONCERNING
PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The State through the government and Regional Government in accordance with their authority is responsible for respecting, protecting, and guaranteeing the human rights of every citizen including women and children without discrimination, because women and children are part of Indonesian citizens who have the same rights as others, and the rights of women and children are human rights that must be guaranteed, protected not only by the government but also by the Regional Government.
Although there are guarantees in laws and regulations that protect citizens, especially women, cases involving women continue to increase, not decrease, because cases of violence against women are like an iceberg phenomenon, namely cases reported to women's protection institutions are only a small part of the actual cases. Women victims of violence often feel hesitant or afraid to report the violence they experience, or there are other obstacles such as difficulty in accessing services and lack of information about their rights because most women victims come from poor and underprivileged families, so they need assistance, assistance costs, and legal consultation are expensive. On the other hand, institutions that handle women's protection are still lacking, especially in areas far from the city center.
Various forms of violence, mistreatment, exploitation, and neglect of Women that occur in the Region require strategic efforts from the Regional Government to provide protection and for women.
Furthermore, in order to realize regional policies to administer governmental affairs that are the authority of the Region in the field of women's protection based on Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government as has been amended several times most recently by Law Number 11 of 2020 concerning Job Creation, it is necessary to formulate this in a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation is a concrete manifestation of the Boyolali Regency Government in providing protection and guaranteeing the fulfillment of the human rights of Women in accordance with its duties and responsibilities.

5.3.rationale: The judge treated references to “kearifan lokal” and “pelestarian adat istiadat” as proof of stakeholder engagement with traditional/cultural actors/mechanisms. In the original Indonesian, Pasal 14 ayat (4) huruf d only says services should “mengakomodasi kearifan lokal” (accommodate local wisdom) in complaint/handling/referral services during disasters; it does not specify engaging customary leaders/institutions. Pasal 18 huruf d mentions “fasilitasi dan upaya pelestarian adat istiadat … untuk kemajuan perempuan,” which is cultural preservation programming, but again not necessarily engagement with traditional/community authorities as stakeholders. Meanwhile, the explicit stakeholder coordination list is in Pasal 32 (coordination with many institutions), but it does not clearly indicate traditional/customary institutions. So the retrieved text did not clearly satisfy the indicator as framed, and the judge over-inferred engagement from cultural references.
